It's highly transparent and people should stop falling for it. And then he shares this tweet from a grandma, Idaho Heartland. Grandma writes, Candace Owens has truly lost her mind.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Neff’s X post, read by Owens, labels her Idaho-event account lies and distortions and forwards a grandparent counteraccount.

records.text: Earlier notice claimed
records.speaker: Handle Idaho Heartland (identity unverified)

appearances.snippet: It's highly transparent and people should stop falling for it. And then he shares this tweet from a grandma, Idaho Heartland. Grandma writes, Candace Owens has truly lost her mind. ... Erika Kirk was at my grandchildren's private school today. Some people are not content unless they are stirring the pot. Okay, quick question: why is she sending her mom a long video? Why don't just go to your mom just call her right up? Send your mom a video just seems like you just facetime your mom. Whatever. Anyway.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The Idaho Heartland grandparent account says it knew of Erika’s visit weeks in advance and denies Owens’s account of student choice and parent notice.

records.text: Newsletter wording presented
records.speaker: Nampa Christian Schools

appearances.snippet: Thursday assembly. Thursday morning, it reads our high school and middle school students at the Flamingo campus will have a special assembly featuring guest speaker Erika Kirk who leads Turning Point Faith. ... She will be sharing with our students about faith and leadership and And it is designed for students. ... Chapel dress is recommended for the day. The event is not being advertised or placed on social media by either NCS or TP Faith.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens reads a newsletter describing a Thursday school assembly for middle- and high-school students, designed for students and not publicly advertised, and says it was received Monday.

records.text: Opt-out process qualified
records.speaker: Nampa Christian parent email author quoted in full (identity unverified)

appearances.snippet: She continues, students were not formally offered an option to opt out. Do you hear that, Andrew (Andrew Kolvet)? You said I was lying about that. ... She continues, parents could independently choose to excuse their children, which is what some parents did. I would like to interject here and to add that we learned that They were then going to be given an absence and some parents could not afford for their kids to be given a man given an absence for having pulled them out because their kids play sports.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: A parent email read by Owens says students were not formally offered an opt-out option but parents could independently excuse children and some did.

records.text: Mixed grades challenge promotion
records.speaker: Nampa Christian parent email author quoted in full (identity unverified)

appearances.snippet: This was not an event that was initiated or organized by the students. TPUSA publicly described the event as quote 500 plus high school students that were attending Club America. ... That was not an accurate description. The assembly included middle school students, so there were not 500 plus high school students in attendance. More importantly, These were not 500 plus students who independently chose or signed up to attend a Club America event. ... They were students attending a school assembly during regular school hours. Andrew (Andrew Kolvet), she's referring to Andrew Kolvet stated that only three students opted out.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The parent email disputes the 500-plus high-school Club America framing because middle-school students attended and the event was a school-hours assembly rather than individual voluntary sign-ups.

records.text: Parent access qualified
records.speaker: Nampa Christian parent email author quoted in full (identity unverified)

appearances.snippet: I also wish to clarify something that could easily be used to dispute the statement that parents are not allowed to attend because there were pictures that were posted after the event that showed that some parents were present. From my understanding, those parents were there because their children were participating or speaking during the event. ... I can't personally verify that. This was the reason that every parent that was pictured was allowed in, but that is my understanding. What I can say is that parents who asked the administrator. ... Administration, if they could attend were told no. The general parent body was never told there was a way to attend or that certain parents would be permitted inside. ... We only discovered afterward through pictures that were being posted that some parents were present. The gym doors were locked during the assembly.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The parent email distinguishes denied requests by the general parent body from photos showing some parents present, offering but not verifying a participation-related explanation for those exceptions.

records.text: Opt-out count disputed
records.speaker: Nampa Christian parent email author quoted in full (identity unverified)

appearances.snippet: I personally know of more than three students who did not attend the assembly. I cannot tell you how he arrived at the number three or exactly what he was counting, but I know for a fact that more than three students did not attend.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The parent email author says they personally know more than three students did not attend but do not know how Kolvet arrived at three or what he counted.

records.text: Confinement inference limited
records.speaker: Nampa Christian parent email author quoted in full (identity unverified)

appearances.snippet: She goes on, I am not suggesting that students were physically trapped inside with no ability to leave under any circumstances. ... I have no reason to believe that a student who needed to use the restroom or had another legitimate reason to leave would not have been allowed out. ... Or had another legitimate reason to leave would not have been allowed out. I am sure there was some type of protocol in place. ... This person, however, goes on and says, but the doors were indeed locked. And as a parent, that raises questions for me.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: The parent email author says locked doors do not mean students were physically trapped without any ability to leave and does not claim legitimate exits were refused.

records.text: Bathroom refusal reports
records.speaker: Nampa Christian bathroom-email parents (identity unverified)

appearances.snippet: I'm going to interject here to offer back that we received two separate emails from parents saying that their children were refused when they asked to use the bathroom. ... I have those emails. So I'm not saying I'll let two parents who emailed and that's why they were upset because their children were refused to use the bathroom because of security protocols.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens interjects that two other parent emails reported their children were refused bathroom access under security protocols, adding conflicting reports to the parent author’s cautious exit account.

records.text: Earlier evidence requested
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I follow the facts. I will make corrections. Look, if granny on X wants to drop an email that was released earlier and show the world that all of these parents that are in our tips box and telling matching stories are lying, then I will concede.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens says she will correct and concede the notice issue if Idaho Heartland produces an earlier email undermining the parents’ matching notice accounts.

records.text: Shared donor alleged
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And I do want to also say to the person who researched and found that there is a very big donor to that school who also donates Turning Point USA. ... Fantastic work. I'm choosing not to name that donor, but there is a financial connection there. It could be coincidental.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens relays an unnamed researcher’s finding of an unnamed major donor shared by Nampa Christian and TPUSA, while acknowledging coincidence is possible.

records.text: Financial influence speculated
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I'm wondering what was behind that push. Obviously, the person who wrote that, I thought very even-keeled email did not explore that possibility, just said that they. ... This was something that they turning point put together. It could be deeper than that. It could the reason why they may have done things they never did before could be most likely is because of some financial incentive in the background. ... Otherwise, you're a school. Why would you want to do that? Why would you want to go against what you've done in the past in terms of allowing students or allowing parents to attend the assembly that feels to me? ... Me like there could potentially be some powerful strings in the background but I'm not stating that factually I'm just giving my opinion and also my assessment as a as a parent I would be very upset and that is why these parents are emailing me I'm not making up the emails so like um yeah.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens speculates that a financial incentive or powerful influence could explain the change in parent assembly access and explicitly labels this her opinion rather than fact.
